title: How much validation evidence does an index selection need? Budget, sampler and the plateau in link-prediction benchmarks

creators.name: Fan, Junkai
creators.affiliation: School of Business Administration, Northeastern University

description:
Replication package for the manuscript "How much validation evidence does an index
selection need? Budget, sampler and the plateau in link-prediction benchmarks"
(Junkai Fan, The Computer Journal, submitted 2026-11-07).

Content of this record
----------------------
data_package.zip   Processed edge lists of the SNAP networks, the three
                   timestamped temporal tables and the eight networks used by
                   the main experiment, with the original SNAP URLs and SHA-256
                   checksums recorded in data/manifest.json.
code_package.zip   Complete code and results: src/ (indices, negative samplers,
                   protocol), scripts/ (experiment drivers, statistics, tables,
                   figures), tables/ and figures/ (the LaTeX sources of every
                   table and every figure), results/ (the CSV/JSON behind every
                   number in the paper), tools/ (the planning tool described in
                   Section 6), docs/ and the frozen configuration.

Reproduction
------------
1. Unpack data_package.zip into the root of the unpacked code_package.zip.
2. pip install -r requirements.txt
3. python scripts/run_experiments.py --workers 6   (~9,660 selections)
4. python scripts/analyze_23networks.py            (pooled table and decay fit)
5. python scripts/analyze_results.py, python scripts/make_figures.py,
   then the make_* scripts in scripts/ for the remaining tables and figures.

The main experiment uses 23 networks: eight SNAP networks, two classical graphs
and thirteen synthetic networks. Florentine, with twenty edges, cannot supply a
balanced validation budget of eight positive pairs and is kept for the
24-network comparison in Appendix A of the paper.
